title: Tibetan medicine Bawei Chenxiang Wan attenuates chronic mountain sickness by targeting the AKT/FOXO3a/CAT axis to inhibit oxidative stress.
authors: Li, Xiaoya; Zhang, Shujing; Qiu, Yuehua; Wang, Yuyan; Hou, Jianchen; Ji, Xuenian; Ge, Fei; Zhang, Xin; Sun, Qingqing; Song, Haochong; Ciwang, Renzeng; Luo, Yamin; Tao, Xiaohua
one_liner_zh: 该文研究藏药BWCX通过AKT/FOXO3a/CAT轴缓解慢性高山病氧化应激，虽涉及FOXO3a与CAT启动子结合及分子对接，但核心是药理机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法以实验为主，AI/物理模拟仅浅层应用。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Bawei Chenxiang Wan (BWCX) is a classical Tibetan medicinal formula originating from the canonical Tibetan medical text The Four Tantras. It is traditionally used to activate qi circulation, nourish the heart, tranquilize the mind and enhance intelligence. It has been applied for over a thousand years on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau to treat cardio-cerebral hypoxic syndromes such as high-altitude (HA) adverse qi flow and mental trance, which are attributed to an imbalance among the three humors (rlung, mkhris-pa, and bad-kan). The traditional applications of BWCX closely align with the clinical manifestations of modern Chronic Mountain Sickness (CMS). However, its effective components and mechanisms of action anti-CMS remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to systematically elucidate the material basis of BWCX anti-CMS and its underlying mechanism of cardio-cerebral protection through the regulation of oxidative stress. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Chemical constituents of BWCX were characterized by UHPLC-MS. To identify core therapeutic targets, we employed network pharmacology and analyzed CMS patient transcriptomes (GSE145774, GSE103940) by combining weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with the random forest (RF) algorithm. Molecular docking was used to validate interactions between active components and predicted targets. A physiologically relevant CMS model was established by exposing 60 mice to a natural HA environment (Lhasa, 3650 m) for 8 weeks. Hematological parameters were measured; oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde [MDA], Catalase [CAT], Total Superoxide Dismutase [T-SOD], glutathione peroxidase [GSH-Px], total antioxidant capacity [T-AOC]) and energy metabolism (adenosine triphosphate [ATP]) in cardiac tissues were assessed by ELISA; and the expression of core targets was analyzed using RT-qPCR and Western blot to verify the regulatory effect of BWCX on the AKT1/FOXO3a/CAT signaling axis, and the binding situation of FOXO3a to the promoter region of CAT was analyzed using ChIP-qPCR to verify the regulatory relationship of FOXO3a on CAT. RESULTS: A total of 78 chemical components were identified, including 18-beta-glycyrrhetinic acid, beta-asarone and quassin. Integrative bioinformatics analysis pinpointed AKT1, FOXO3 and CAT as core targets of BWCX anti-CMS, with significant enrichment in oxidative stress-related pathways. Molecular docking results showed that the binding energies of costunolide with AKT1, FOXO3a, CAT and ESR2 were -9.5, -8.8, -11.1 and -9.9 kcal/mol, respectively; while those of 18-beta-glycyrrhetinic acid with the above targets were -9.1, -8.2, -10.2 and -9.2 kcal/mol, respectively, indicating their strong potential for target binding. Animal experiments demonstrated that BWCX intervention significantly reversed CMS-induced hematological abnormalities [increased red blood cells (RBC), hemoglobin (HGB), hematocrit (HCT) and platelets (PLT)], ameliorated cardiac oxidative stress (reduced MDA; elevated T-AOC, T-SOD, GSH-Px, CAT, ATP), and corrected the dysregulated molecular expression: it suppressed the upregulation of AKT1 mRNA/protein and p-AKT1/AKT1 ratio, while restoring the downregulated mRNA/protein expression of FOXO3a and CAT and the p-FOXO3a/FOXO3a ratio in cardiac and hippocampal tissues (P < 0.05). RT-qPCR analysis of AKT1, FOXO3a, and CAT mRNA expression in vitro revealed trends consistent with those observed in the in vivo experiments. It was also verified that significant enrichment of FOXO3a was detected in the CAT promoter region under hypoxic stress (P < 0.05). FOXO3a binds to the CAT promoter in H9C2 cells, thereby confirming that CAT is a direct transcriptional target of FOXO3a. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first evidence that BWCX alleviates CMS-induced cardio-cerebral hypoxic injury by modulating the AKT1/FOXO3a/CAT signaling axis, thereby rebalancing oxidative stress and improving hemorheology. These findings provide a modern pharmacological interpretation of its traditional cardiocerebral protective effect, offer a paradigm for ethnomedicine research modernization, and lay a scientific foundation for its clinical application and quality control.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：八味沉香丸（BWCX）是一种经典藏药方剂，源自藏医经典著作《四部医典》。传统上用于行气、养心、安神益智。在青藏高原已应用逾千年，用于治疗心脑缺氧综合征，如高原（HA）逆气扰动和神志恍惚，这些病症归因于三种体液（隆、赤巴、培根）失衡。BWCX的传统应用与现代慢性高原病（CMS）的临床表现高度契合。然而，其抗CMS的有效成分和作用机制尚不明确。研究目的：本研究旨在系统阐明BWCX抗CMS的物质基础及其通过调节氧化应激实现心脑保护的内在机制。材料与方法：采用UHPLC-MS对BWCX的化学成分进行表征。为识别核心治疗靶点，我们运用网络药理学，并结合加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）与随机森林（RF）算法，分析了CMS患者转录组数据（GSE145774、GSE103940）。采用分子对接验证活性成分与预测靶点之间的相互作用。通过将60只小鼠暴露于自然高原环境（拉萨，海拔3650米）8周，建立了生理相关的CMS模型。测量血液学参数；采用ELISA评估心脏组织中的氧化应激标志物（丙二醛[MDA]、过氧化氢酶[CAT]、总超氧化物歧化酶[T-SOD]、谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶[GSH-Px]、总抗氧化能力[T-AOC]）和能量代谢（三磷酸腺苷[ATP]）；利用RT-qPCR和Western blot分析核心靶点的表达，以验证BWCX对AKT1/FOXO3a/CAT信号轴的调节作用，并使用ChIP-qPCR分析FOXO3a与CAT启动子区的结合情况，以验证FOXO3a对CAT的调控关系。结果：共鉴定出78种化学成分，包括18-β-甘草次酸、β-细辛醚和苦木素。综合生物信息学分析确定AKT1、FOXO3和CAT为BWCX抗CMS的核心靶点，并在氧化应激相关通路中显著富集。分子对接结果显示，木香烃内酯与AKT1、FOXO3a、CAT和ESR2的结合能分别为-9.5、-8.8、-11.1和-9.9 kcal/mol；而18-β-甘草次酸与上述靶点的结合能分别为-9.1、-8.2、-10.2和-9.2 kcal/mol，表明其具有强大的靶点结合潜力。动物实验表明，BWCX干预显著逆转了CMS诱导的血液学异常[红细胞（RBC）、血红蛋白（HGB）、红细胞压积（HCT）和血小板（PLT）升高]，改善了心脏氧化应激（降低MDA；升高T-AOC、T-SOD、GSH-Px、CAT、ATP），并纠正了失调的分子表达：它抑制了AKT1 mRNA/蛋白及p-AKT1/AKT1比值的上调，同时恢复了心脏和海马组织中FOXO3a和CAT的mRNA/蛋白表达及p-FOXO3a/FOXO3a比值的下调（P < 0.05）。体外RT-qPCR分析AKT1、FOXO3a和CAT mRNA表达，其趋势与体内实验观察结果一致。同时验证了在低氧应激下，FOXO3a在CAT启动子区域显著富集（P < 0.05）。FOXO3a与H9C2细胞中的CAT启动子结合，从而证实CAT是FOXO3a的直接转录靶点。结论：本研究首次证明BWCX通过调节AKT1/FOXO3a/CAT信号轴，从而重新平衡氧化应激和改善血液流变学，缓解CMS诱导的心脑缺氧损伤。这些发现为其传统心脑保护作用提供了现代药理学解释，为民族药物研究现代化提供了范式，并为其临床应用和质量控制奠定了科学基础。
